items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Another time I went with Dany Doris, a talented young vibraphonist.

ctx.x: It was a big change for us but time didn't stand still.

I went back different times to the Chikito in Switzerland, the caberet where I had met Lily in 1950. I went there with different French group that I had formed. Once with Guy Lafitte who had become the best French tenor sax, a real disciple of Hawkins. Another time I went with Dany Doris, a talented young vibraphonist. As I had been nominated Honourary president of the Jazz Club of Zurich, I would often have visits at the Chikito from groups of members of the jazz club, which visits would delight me.

In May 1965, I played there for a month and the boss asked me if it would be alright if he engaged the violinist Stuff Smith for 15 days to play as an added attraction with me and my group. Of course I agreed. I knew Stuff from way back and liked his hard swinging and groovy style. That man could swing like nobody else. Unfortunately he was in a bad state of health, suffering with stomach ulcers. He was not supposed to drink at all but couldn't help from having whiskey that he would dilute with plenty of water.…
